primary_meaning: Life, flourishing, rootedness, and fruitfulness under God. In Christian teaching, a thriving tree commonly represents a person or community sustained by God and producing good fruit; the tree of life intensifies this symbolism into divine or eternal life.
primary_basis: Genesis 2:9; 3:22–24 — the tree of life in Eden
Psalm 1:1–3 — the righteous person as a tree planted by streams, bearing fruit
Proverbs 3:18; 11:30; 13:12; 15:4 — wisdom and righteousness described as a tree of life
Jeremiah 17:7–8 — the person who trusts in the Lord as a fruitful, well-watered tree
Ezekiel 47:12 — life-giving trees whose fruit is food and leaves bring healing
Matthew 7:17–20; 12:33 — trees and fruit as images of character and conduct
Revelation 2:7; 22:1–2,14 — the tree of life associated with paradise, healing, and eternal life

alternatives.meaning: An individual person, ruler, nation, or empire, especially one characterized by stature, influence, prosperity, or downfall.
basis: Judges 9:7–15 — trees represent rulers in Jotham’s parable
Psalm 37:35 — the wicked person compared to a flourishing tree
Ezekiel 17:22–24; 31:3–14 — trees symbolize kingdoms and imperial power
Daniel 4:10–27 — the great tree represents Nebuchadnezzar and his kingdom

alternatives.meaning: God’s kingdom growing from small beginnings into expansive shelter.
basis: Matthew 13:31–32; Mark 4:30–32; Luke 13:18–19 — the mustard seed becomes a tree in which birds nest
Ezekiel 17:22–24 — God plants a lofty tree that shelters birds

alternatives.meaning: Moral character revealed by its fruit; a good or bad tree represents a good or corrupt person, teacher, or community.
basis: Jude 12 — fruitless trees used for condemned teachers

alternatives.meaning: Israel or the covenant people, often represented by an olive tree or fig tree and subject to cultivation, pruning, judgment, or restoration.
basis: Hosea 9:10,16 — Israel likened to fruit and a stricken root
Matthew 21:18–22; Mark 11:12–21 — the barren fig tree, commonly read in relation to Israel or its leadership
Romans 11:16–24 — cultivated and wild olive branches representing covenant inclusion and exclusion

alternatives.meaning: The cross of Christ, especially when New Testament texts call the instrument of crucifixion a 'tree'; later Christian tradition also contrasts the cross with Eden’s trees.
basis: Deuteronomy 21:22–23 — one hanged on a tree is under a curse

alternatives.meaning: Forbidden knowledge, disobedience, and humanity’s attempt to determine good and evil apart from God, specifically through the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
Judgment, barrenness, mortality, or destruction when a tree is fruitless, cut down, uprooted, or withered.
Wisdom or Torah as a source of life and blessing.
basis: Psalm 1:1–3, often interpreted in relation to meditation on God’s law

notes: There is no single settled symbolic meaning for the generic term 'tree.' Its meaning is strongly controlled by context, species, condition, and narrative role. Life and fruitful flourishing are the broadest positive associations, but Scripture also regularly uses trees for persons, kingdoms, Israel, moral character, the cross, forbidden knowledge, and judgment.
